caution: A failure to reproduce is not a finding that the paper is wrong. It may be a failure of the attempt.

attempts.label: DANDI:000059
attempts.paper_title: Cooling of Medial Septum Reveals Theta Phase Lag Coordination of Hippocampal Cell Assemblies
attempts.entry_title: Cooling of the medial septum, hippocampal theta and place cell timing (Petersen & Buzsaki 2020)
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Petersen and Buzsaki (2020) on dandiset 000059, which holds 50 sessions of five rats running a spatial alternation task on a figure-8 maze while the medial septum was cooled, with MS temperature, trials, position, LFP, wide-band data and sorted units. It tests the slowing of theta with temperature, the increase of choice errors, the oscillation frequency of place cells against LFP theta, place field features, and the time and phase lags of place cell pairs. The hippocampal temperature recordings of the control experiment are not in the dandiset.

outcomes.statement: A session holds about 40 control trials, 20 to 60 cooling trials and 20 to 80 recovery trials, 80 to 200 trials in all with a mean of 150.
outcomes.source: Results, MS cooling decreases hippocampal theta frequency and power, paragraph 2; STAR Methods, Electrophysiological Recordings
outcomes.quote: After a block of control trials (~ 40 trials) ... about 20 to 60 ‘cooling’ trials), followed by recovery trials (20 to 80) ... a total number of trials ranging from 80 to 200 (mean: 150 trials).
outcomes.notes: Over 45 BEH sessions the mean is 143.8 trials (80 to 204); medians of 39 pre-cooling, 47 cooling and 44 post-cooling trials. 12 sessions have two cooling blocks, which the paper does not mention; in each the second block follows post-cooling trials, and the onset-aligned series stops before it. 'Cooling off' trials (median 14 per session) are counted in no state.
deviations: 45 of the paper's 53 sessions.

outcomes.statement: MS cooling peaked about 60 s after its onset and lasted about 10 to 12 minutes.
outcomes.source: STAR Methods, Electrophysiological Recordings
outcomes.quote: The cooling typically peaked after about 60 sec after the cooling onset (suppl. fig. 1G) and lasted for about 10–12 minutes
outcomes.notes: Over 37 sessions with a recorded temperature the minimum comes a median 121 s after the onset (IQR 89 to 138 s; 119 to 122 s for onset thresholds of 0.5 to 2 C), against 60 s. The duration holds under reading (b), 12.16 minutes until the temperature is within 1 C of baseline; under reading (a) the temperature is below 32 C for 8.77 minutes. The median minimum is 21.2 C. The drop is fast and the temperature then stays near its minimum, so the time to the minimum overstates the time to the peak effect. 90% of each session's drop is reached a median 53 s after onset (IQR 44 to 63 s), and the onset-aligned mean trace is within 0.5 C of its minimum from 70 to 152 s. Without the five sessions whose baseline has artefacts above 38 C or whose onset is detected early, the values are 121.5 s and 12.22 minutes.
deviations: The onset is taken from the temperature trace (1 C below the pre-cooling median), as the files have no time of dry-ice placement; the Methods do not define the onset.

outcomes.statement: Theta frequency decreased linearly with MS temperature (R = 0.81, P = 5.4e-48).
outcomes.source: Results, MS cooling decreases hippocampal theta frequency and power, paragraph 2; Figure 2G
outcomes.quote: Theta frequency decreased linearly with MS temperature (Figure 2g; down to 20° C; R = 0.81
outcomes.notes: With the code's aligned series, R = 0.789 (P = 2.8e-43, 198 positions) over 37 TEMP sessions under reading (a), and R = 0.758 (P = 3e-38) with the MS10 temperature curves under reading (b); both are within tolerance. Over single trials pooled R = 0.672, slope 0.065 Hz per C. Per rat R is 0.685 to 0.954.
deviations: 37 sessions with a recorded temperature, where the paper used 53; the MS10 temperature in the dandiset is not a recording.
The theta electrode is the one flagged theta_reference in the files; the code's channel numbers could not be mapped to the files' electrodes.

outcomes.statement: Theta power also decreased with MS temperature, less tightly than frequency (R = 0.54, P = 1.2e-16).
outcomes.source: Results, MS cooling decreases hippocampal theta frequency and power, paragraph 2; Figure 2H
outcomes.quote: this relationship was more consistent across animals than the effect on theta power (R = 0.54
outcomes.notes: Theta power does not follow temperature, R = -0.056 (P = 0.44) over TEMP sessions and R = 0.123 (P = 0.085) with the MS10 curves; over single trials pooled R = 0.107. Power is the spectrogram magnitude of the band-passed LFP as in calcInstantaneousTheta.m, minus each session's mean, at frames above 30 cm/s, and the 10 cm/s variant gives R = 0.135. Per rat the power R ranges from -0.346 to 0.376.
deviations: The theta electrode is the one flagged theta_reference in the files, which may differ from the paper's; power depends on the electrode more than frequency does. The LFP column read is that row in every session (checked through the LFP electrodes region).
Power is taken from the spectrogram of the 4 to 10 Hz band-passed LFP, as in the paper's code (calcInstantaneousTheta.m); the band-pass weights frequencies within the band unequally.

outcomes.statement: The relationship of theta frequency with MS temperature was more consistent across animals than that of theta power.
outcomes.source: Results, MS cooling decreases hippocampal theta frequency and power, paragraph 2; Figure 2J
outcomes.quote: Theta frequency decreased linearly with MS temperature ... and this relationship was more consistent across animals than the effect on theta power
outcomes.notes: In each of the four rats with a recorded temperature the frequency R is positive (0.685 to 0.954, every P below 1e-22), a range of 0.269, against a range of 0.722 for power (-0.346 to 0.376). The outcome rests on power varying across rats, since power shows no consistent effect (fig2h-theta-power-temperature).
deviations: Four rats; MS10 has no recorded temperature.

outcomes.statement: Theta frequency and power were lower during MS cooling than before and after it.
outcomes.source: Figure 2I; Results, MS cooling decreases hippocampal theta frequency and power, paragraph 2
outcomes.quote: MS cooling induced fast and reversible change in the frequency and power of hippocampal theta oscillations (Figure 2d, e, f, i).
outcomes.notes: Frequency is lower during cooling than before (44 of 45 sessions, P = 1.4e-12) and after (45 of 45, P = 5.7e-14). Power is lower than before at P = 0.048 (26 of 45) but not lower than after (19 of 45, P = 0.94); during cooling it is 0.972 of the session mean of the three states.
deviations: State means over trials, from the dandiset's labels, with 'Cooling off' trials left out.

outcomes.statement: During MS cooling LFP theta frequency decreased by 12%.
outcomes.source: Discussion, Theta phase organization of hippocampal cell assemblies, paragraph 5
outcomes.quote: During MS cooling, LFP theta frequency decreased by 12 %
outcomes.notes: The decrease is 8.88% (a), 9.18% (b) and 9.23% (c), none within 12 +- 1.2%. The slowest cooling trial of a session is a mean 16.93% below pre. Per rat 4.76% (MS12) to 10.74% (MS21). The paper's within-field values (8.4 and 7.7 Hz) are reproduced in fig4b-fp-flfp-decrease.
deviations: The paper does not say how the 12% is computed; three readings were tested.

outcomes.statement: MS cooling increased choice errors about 3-fold, within each rat (P < 0.05 for all animals) and across all animals (P = 1e-6).
outcomes.source: Results, MS cooling increases behavioral errors, paragraph 1; Figure 6D and 6E
outcomes.quote: Overall, the number of memory errors increased approximately 3-fold, assessed either within rats (P < 0.05 for all animals) or across all animals
outcomes.notes: Errors are 6.67% before and 15.23% during cooling (40 of 45 sessions higher, P = 3e-07), ratios 2.28 (a), 2.31 (b) and 2.53 (c), all below 2.7. Per rat, P = 0.0078 (MS10), 0.039 (MS12), 0.027 (MS21) and 0.064 (MS22, 10 of 12 higher); MS13 has 5 sessions, all higher (P = 0.0625, the smallest possible). Counting 'Cooling off' trials as cooling gives a ratio of 1.98; TEMP sessions alone 1.96.
deviations: States from the dandiset's trial labels; the code counts errors by time windows from the cooling onsets and offsets, which are not in the files.
45 of 53 sessions; MS13 has 5 sessions here, too few for an exact signed-rank test to reach 0.05.

outcomes.statement: The error rate after cooling did not differ from the error rate before it.
outcomes.source: Figure 6E (marked ns)
outcomes.quote: Choice errors shown as boxplots constructed from all sessions. ... ns = nonsignificant.
outcomes.notes: Post 6.49% against pre 6.67% (median difference -0.13 points, P = 0.837, 45 sessions); cooling against post P = 8e-08.
deviations: The figure's 'ns' was read as pre against post.

outcomes.statement: The worst memory performance occurred between trials 4 and 8 after the onset of cooling, when MS temperature reached its minimum.
outcomes.source: Results, MS cooling increases behavioral errors, paragraph 1; Figure 6C
outcomes.quote: The worst memory performance occurred between trials 4 and 8 after MS cooling, when the MS temperature reached its minimum
outcomes.notes: The mean smoothed error series over 45 sessions peaks at trial 7 after onset (0.193, against 0.066 over the 40 trials before), the trial of the minimum mean temperature and theta frequency. The peak is narrow and the result fragile. A second rise reaches 0.186 at trial 20, and within single rats the mean peaks later, at trials 14 to 26. All 45 sessions contribute at every trial from 1 to 40.

outcomes.statement: The incidence of errors correlated negatively with MS temperature (R = -0.35, P < 0.01).
outcomes.source: Results, MS cooling increases behavioral errors, paragraph 1; Figure 6F
outcomes.quote: The incidence of errors negatively and significantly correlated with temperature change (R = − 0.35; P < 0.01; all animals)
outcomes.notes: Negative and stronger than reported, R = -0.838 (a, P = 5.9e-41), -0.789 (b) and -0.868 (c), none within -0.35 +- 0.035. Over single trials pooled R = -0.127 (P = 5.5e-20); per rat -0.298 to -0.860. The paper's value may come from a different unit of analysis, which its text does not give.
deviations: 37 sessions with a recorded temperature.

outcomes.statement: The incidence of errors correlated negatively with theta frequency (R = -0.35, P < 0.01).
outcomes.source: Results, MS cooling increases behavioral errors, paragraph 1; Figure 6G
outcomes.quote: The incidence of errors negatively and significantly correlated with ... theta frequency (R = − 0.35; P < 0.01; all animals)

outcomes.statement: The incidence of errors correlated less with theta power; only 2 of 5 animals had a significant correlation (R beyond -0.3, P < 0.01).
outcomes.source: Results, MS cooling increases behavioral errors, paragraph 1; Figure 6H and 6J
outcomes.quote: The incidence of errors negatively and significantly correlated with ... and less so with theta power (only 2 of 5 animals had significant R > − 0.3; P < 0.01)
outcomes.notes: One rat counts (MS10, R = -0.425, P = 1.1e-09). MS21 is significant with R = -0.202 (P = 0.0063), and MS22 with the opposite sign (R = 0.325, P = 1.2e-05).

outcomes.statement: The incidence of errors did not correlate with the running speed of the rat (R about 0.1, P > 0.05 for all animals).
outcomes.source: Results, MS cooling increases behavioral errors, paragraph 1; Figure 6I and 6J
outcomes.quote: The incidence of errors negatively and significantly correlated with ... and not with the running speed of the rat (R ~ 0.1; P > 0.05 for all animals
outcomes.notes: Three of five rats have P < 0.05, MS13 (R = -0.493, P = 8e-11), MS21 (R = 0.216, P = 0.0034) and MS22 (R = 0.247, P = 0.001); MS10 and MS12 do not (P = 0.32 and 0.49). Over all sessions together R = 0.093 (P = 0.19). The correlations are over about 150 to 190 aligned positions, so small R values reach significance.

outcomes.statement: Running speed decreased relatively monotonically within a session.
outcomes.source: Results, Effects of MS cooling on single neuron properties, paragraph 3; Figure 4E and 6C
outcomes.quote: Running speed decreased relatively monotonically within session (Fig. 4e; see also Fig. 5c).
outcomes.notes: Speed falls with trial number in 44 of 45 sessions (median rho -0.452, P = 4e-13), in every rat; the aligned mean falls from 86.0 to 73.7 cm/s.

outcomes.statement: Mean running speed was 87.3 +- 8.0 cm/s in control trials and 86.2 +- 9.9 cm/s during MS cooling.
outcomes.source: Results, MS temperature effects on theta time/phase compression of place cells sequences, paragraph 2
outcomes.quote: we combined trials before and after cooling into a single control group (mean running speed = 87.3±8.0). During MS cooling (mean running speed = 86.2±9.9)
outcomes.notes: Over 15 sessions, reading (a) gives control 78.9 and cooling 74.9 cm/s, both outside; reading (b) gives control 79.6, within 87.3 +- 8.0, and cooling 76.0, 0.3 cm/s below 86.2 +- 9.9. The criterion needs both values within tolerance under one reading, and neither reading gives both. Speed is lower during cooling than in control (P = 0.035 to 0.041).
deviations: 15 of the code's 18 Figure 5 sessions; the paper does not define its speed measure.

outcomes.statement: Within-field and peak firing rates of place cells decreased moderately during MS cooling (11% and 12%; P < 1e-9 and P < 1e-11).
outcomes.source: Results, Effects of MS cooling on single neuron properties, paragraph 2 (Supplementary Figure 2)
outcomes.quote: Both within-field and peak firing rates of place cells decreased moderately during MS cooling (Suppl. Fig. 2; 11% and 12%
outcomes.notes: Over 636 fields both rates fall (P = 0.0024 and 0.0013), by 3.7% and 5.3% as medians (a), 7.7% and 6.7% as ratios of means (b); reading (c) is dominated by fields with near-zero pre rates (-111% and -70%). Fields with at least 50 spikes in each state give 10.8% and 9.9%. The decrease differs between rats (MS12 rises by 10.1%, MS13 falls by 27.8%).
deviations: Place fields by the automatic criteria of the Methods for Figure 5; the paper defined the fields of this analysis by hand.
Putative pyramidal cells typed here from waveforms and rates; the files have no cell types.

outcomes.statement: Firing rates of interneurons decreased during MS cooling by about 14%.
outcomes.source: Discussion, Theta phase organization of hippocampal cell assemblies, paragraph 5; Results, Effects of MS cooling on single neuron properties, paragraph 2
outcomes.quote: During MS cooling, LFP theta frequency decreased by 12 % and within-field firing rates of place cells decreased by a similar proportion (12%; interneurons 14%).
outcomes.notes: 127 putative interneurons, lower in 75 (P = 0.0017), by 6.5% (a) or 9.1% (b); thresholds of 0.35 and 0.5 ms, and narrow units alone, give 9.4% to 9.9%.
deviations: Putative interneurons typed here (trough-to-peak at most 0.425 ms, or above 10 Hz).

outcomes.statement: The theta oscillation frequency of putative fast-spiking interneurons decreased during MS cooling, commensurate with the LFP theta.
outcomes.source: Results, Effects of MS cooling on single neuron properties, paragraph 1 (Supplementary Figure 2D)
outcomes.quote: Theta frequency oscillation of putative fast spiking interneurons also decelerated (Suppl. Fig. 2d), commensurate with the downward frequency shift of LFP theta oscillation.
outcomes.notes: 9.55 to 8.66 Hz (lower in 105 of 114, P = 8.7e-16), a 9.4% decrease against 8.8% for the LFP theta of the same sessions; narrow units alone P = 3.1e-11.
deviations: Putative interneurons typed here; the paper's fast-spiking interneurons come from CellExplorer.

outcomes.statement: The waveforms of hippocampal action potentials were not affected by MS cooling.
outcomes.source: Results, MS cooling decreases hippocampal theta frequency and power, paragraph 3 (Supplementary Figure 1G)
outcomes.quote: Finally, the waveforms of action potentials in the hippocampus ... were not affected by MS cooling (Suppl. Fig. 1g).
outcomes.notes: Over 646 units, trough-to-peak differs (P = 4.9e-10, median change 0 as most units do not move by a whole 0.05 ms sample) and amplitude rises by a median 0.8% (P = 0.00057). The windows start 7.1 to 31.8 minutes apart (5.1 to 29.8 minutes from the end of the pre window), so drift cannot be separated from cooling; for interneurons alone neither differs (P = 0.066 and 0.2). Fewer spikes are averaged in the cooling window (median 200 against 247.5), but in the 208 units whose two means both use the 300-spike cap the changes remain (amplitude 0.7%, P = 0.032; trough-to-peak P = 2.2e-05), so the spike count does not explain them. The effect is small, and the outcome follows the paper's test as written; it does not show that cooling changes the waveforms.
deviations: Waveforms from 120 s windows of the wide-band data at 20 kHz, high-passed at 300 Hz, on the channel of largest amplitude; the paper's measure is in its supplement, which could not be read.

outcomes.statement: MS cooling decreased both the oscillation frequency of place cells (fp) and the LFP theta frequency in their fields (fLFP) by about the same degree, and both recovered (fLFP 8.4, 7.7, 8.5 Hz; fp 10.6, 9.5, 10.4 Hz before, during and after; n = 365).
outcomes.source: Results, Effects of MS cooling on single neuron properties, paragraph 2; Figure 4B
outcomes.quote: MS cooling decreased both fp and fLFP, measured within the place fields of neurons, by approximately the same degree ... Both values recovered after cooling.
outcomes.notes: Over 361 fields (paper 365) all six means are within the paper's spreads; fp falls in 311 (P = 3.5e-44) and fLFP in 352 (P = 1.2e-60), by 9.2% and 9.0%, and both recover. Each rat shows the same pattern and every session the decrease; in MS22-180720-110055 fp does not recover (9.92 Hz after, 10.15 Hz during cooling). Fields with at least 100 or 200 spikes per state give the same means.
deviations: Fields by the automatic criteria of the Methods, from 11 sessions in 4 rats.

outcomes.statement: fp and fLFP were correlated across place fields before, during and after cooling (R = 0.61, 0.59 and 0.36; P < 1e-6 each).
outcomes.source: Figure 4C
outcomes.quote: Correlation between LFP theta frequency (fLFP) and place cell oscillation frequency (fp; Rpre = 0.61; Rcooling = 0.59; Rpost = 036
outcomes.notes: All positive (P = 1.5e-05, 6.7e-19 and 0.0029) and weaker than 0.61, 0.59 and 0.36; within rats R ranges from -0.05 to 0.64.

outcomes.statement: During MS cooling fp and fLFP decreased in parallel, so the difference fp - fLFP remained constant.
outcomes.source: Results, Effects of MS cooling on single neuron properties, paragraph 2; Discussion, Theta phase organization of hippocampal cell assemblies, paragraph 3
outcomes.quote: during MS cooling fp and fLFP decreased proportionally (i.e., fp–fLFP difference remained constant)
outcomes.notes: fp - fLFP falls from 2.009 to 1.806 Hz (median change -0.128 Hz, P = 0.000132, 361 fields) and stays at 1.790 Hz after cooling; the ratio fp/fLFP is preserved (1.237 and 1.232, P = 0.84). By rat the mean change is -1.03 Hz (MS12), 0.01 (MS13), -0.19 (MS21) and 0.10 (MS22).
deviations: The paper names no test; its default paired test was used.

outcomes.statement: fLFP and fp measured within place fields decreased linearly with MS temperature (fLFP R = 0.66, slope 0.071 Hz per C; fp R = 0.38, slope 0.09 Hz per C).
outcomes.source: Results, Effects of MS cooling on single neuron properties, paragraph 1; Figure 4A
outcomes.quote: The theta oscillation frequency of pyramidal neurons decreased linearly and paralleled the downward frequency shift of LFP theta oscillation (Fig. 4a; fLFP: R = 0.66, Slope = 0.071. fp: R = 0.38, slope = 0.09).
outcomes.notes: Over 52474 windows from 563 fields, fLFP R = 0.678 and slope 0.0716 Hz per C, fp slope 0.0859, within tolerance; fp R = 0.338, just below 0.342. The windows overlap (stepped by one trial), so the P values over windows overstate the evidence; the paper's code does the same.
deviations: Windows of 20 trials stepped by one trial, as calc_trial_averages.m; the paper's figure does not say which windows it plots.

outcomes.statement: Place field size was highly correlated before and during MS cooling (R = 0.91).
outcomes.source: Results, Effect of MS cooling on place field features, paragraph 1; Figure 3C
outcomes.quote: Place field size does not change with MS cooling (R = 0.91).
outcomes.notes: R = 0.8197 over 635 fields, at the edge of the tolerance (0.819). With at least 20 or 50 spikes per state R is 0.8348 and 0.8308, with at least 100 it is 0.8136, outside. Sizes do not differ (62.7 and 64.9 cm, P = 0.084).
deviations: Field size from rate maps of each state (bins above 10% of the peak); the paper does not define it.

outcomes.statement: Place field size and fp were negatively correlated before, during and after cooling (R = -0.49, -0.40, -0.40; P < 1e-9).
outcomes.source: Figure 3D
outcomes.quote: Place field size continues to be inversely correlated with fp after MS cooling (Rpre = − 0.49; Rcooling = − 0.40; Rpost = − 0.40
outcomes.notes: All negative with P below 3e-09, weaker than -0.49 and -0.40.

outcomes.statement: Measured place field size correlated with the size predicted by SPF = v / (fp - fLFP) before (R = 0.55) and during (R = 0.54) cooling, and weakly after (R = 0.11).
outcomes.source: Results, Effect of MS cooling on place field features, paragraph 2; Figure 3E
outcomes.quote: We found a reliable and similar relationships between measured place field sizes and model-predicted sizes for trials before (R = 0.55), during (R = 0.54) and after (R = 0.11) MS cooling (Fig. 3e).
outcomes.notes: Pre and cooling positive (P = 4.7e-06 and 4.9e-11) and weaker than 0.55 and 0.54; post 0.325 against 0.11. Predicted sizes (median 47 to 48 cm) are smaller than measured (65 cm).

outcomes.statement: The information content of place cell spikes was not altered by MS cooling (P > 0.26).
outcomes.source: Figure 3F; Results, Effect of MS cooling on place field features, paragraph 2
outcomes.quote: Information content of place cell spikes was also left unaltered by MS cooling (P > 0.26; Fig. 3f).
outcomes.notes: Over 374 place cells information is lower during cooling than before (median change -0.029 against a median of 1.253 bits/spike, P = 0.014) and lower after than before (P = 0.0064); cooling and post do not differ (P = 0.31). The changes are small. Bits per spike rise when fewer spikes are used, and the pre state has the fewest trials, but with each state's spikes subsampled to the same count (360 cells) pre against cooling gives P = 0.0073 and pre against post P = 0.0092, so the decrease does not come from the spike counts.
deviations: The paper names its comparisons but not its test; its default paired test was used.

outcomes.statement: The spatial scale of the population vector correlation of pyramidal cells was not affected by MS cooling.
outcomes.source: Results, Effect of MS cooling on place field features, paragraph 3; Figure 3H and 3I
outcomes.quote: Population vector correlation of pyramidal cells was not affected by MS cooling (Fig. 3g, h).
outcomes.notes: Median change 0.25 cm, P = 0.966 over 11 sessions (paper 21); scales 18.3 to 36.9 cm.
deviations: The decorrelation scale is computed within maze segments at 5 cm bins; 11 sessions.

outcomes.statement: The phase precession slope decreased slightly but significantly during MS cooling (P < 0.007 and P < 0.0003).
outcomes.source: Results, Effects of MS cooling on single neuron properties, paragraph 2; Figure 4D
outcomes.quote: The slope of the relationship between travel distance across the place field and phase advancement of spikes ... decreased slightly, but nevertheless significantly, during MS cooling (Fig. 4d).
outcomes.notes: Under reading (a), the slope magnitude during cooling does not differ from pre (median change 0, P = 0.83) and is smaller than post (P = 0.022); under (b) neither comparison differs (P = 0.32 and 0.15). 87.5% of fields have a negative slope before cooling.
deviations: The direction of 'decreased' is not stated; two readings were tested.
Slopes by a grid search of circular-linear regression up to two cycles per field.

outcomes.statement: fp depended on running speed more strongly than fLFP, and fp during cooling was lower at all velocities.
outcomes.source: Results, Effects of MS cooling on single neuron properties, paragraph 3; Figure 4G and 4H
outcomes.quote: fp values during cooling were lower at all velocities (Fig. 4g) ... while speed exerted a relatively linear effect on fp, it had no or little effect on the frequency of fLFP
outcomes.notes: fp slope 0.0136 Hz per cm/s (P = 3.2e-12), fLFP 0.0061; difference 0.0074 (bootstrap interval 0.0040 to 0.0112). In the three speed bins from 60 to 120 cm/s with at least 10 fields fp is lower during cooling (P below 1e-5 each); below 60 cm/s too few fields had 50 spikes.
deviations: Speed bins of 20 cm/s; the paper's bins are not stated.

outcomes.statement: The theta-repeated cross-correlograms of place cell pairs had a period of about 85 ms before cooling, which lengthened during MS cooling (P = 0.002), while the period of the phase cross-correlograms was unaffected (P = 0.32).
outcomes.source: Figure 5D, 5E and 5F
outcomes.quote: Duration of the theta-repeated spike cross-correlograms (as in d), calculated for each session, significantly increased during MS cooling ... whereas the spike phase-lag correlations remained unaffected (n.s., P = 0.32).

statistics.about: period of the time cross-correlograms, cooling against control
period of the phase cross-correlograms, cooling against control

outcomes.notes: Over 9 sessions the period lengthens from 109.2 to 114.0 ms (8 of 9, P = 0.0195) and the phase period does not change (1.740 and 1.760 pi rad, P = 0.59); the control period is not 85 +- 8.5 ms. The criterion's estimator takes the largest neighbouring peak 60 to 200 ms from the main peak, and in 47.7% of pre pairs that peak is more than 1.25 times as far as the nearest one, so it often picks the second neighbour and the 109.2 ms is biased upward. With the nearest neighbouring peak (a variant) the control period is 91.0 ms, within tolerance, and it lengthens to 95.5 ms (7 of 9, P = 0.031); pairs with |Ltr| below 10 cm give 91.0 ms. Under that variant the phase period, also from the nearest peak, does not change (1.285 pi rad in both, P = 0.367), so all three parts of the criterion hold; but that estimator is biased downward, as 211 of 3499 pre pairs give 60 to 70 ms, at the floor of the search window and below any plausible theta period, so its 91.0 ms is not a clean test of 85 ms either. The outcome follows the criterion's estimator. Both control periods are shorter than the LFP theta period (115.7 ms).
deviations: The period is measured per pair and summarised per session; the paper reads it from the sum over pairs. The criterion was changed to this before the analysis across sessions, after a pilot session showed that the summed correlogram's spectrum follows its envelope; the summed correlogram is shown as a variant (99 to 200 ms).
9 sessions in 4 rats, against 18 in 5.
The criterion's period estimator often takes the second neighbouring peak; the nearest-peak estimator is shown as a variant.

outcomes.statement: Distance-time compression of place cell pairs (0.54 cm/ms before cooling) decreased during MS cooling (P = 0.02), while distance-phase compression was unchanged (P = 0.92).
outcomes.source: Figure 5C and 5G; Results, MS temperature effects on theta time/phase compression of place cells sequences, paragraph 2
outcomes.quote: Compression index, c (cm/ms; i.e., the slope in c), significantly decreased during MS cooling (* P = 0.02) but the distance/phase lag compression (cm/radian) remained unaffected (P = 0.92).
outcomes.notes: Pooled pre compression 0.273 cm/ms against 0.54. Per session it is lower during cooling in 8 of 9 sessions without significance (0.298 against 0.191, P = 0.0547); phase compression does not change (P = 0.426). Lag and distance correlate weakly (R = 0.195), so the slope depends on the fit (inverse regression over pooled pre pairs 7.175 cm/ms). The 70 ms window can hold more than one candidate peak; in 10.5% of pre pairs the lag changes when the window is narrowed to half the theta period, which gives 0.156 cm/ms. The compression magnitude cannot be judged from this method. The direction of the change agrees with the paper under the criterion's fit; the inverse slope goes the other way (control 9.085, cooling 10.420 cm/ms, lower in 1 of 9).
deviations: Lags from each pair's correlogram peak and compression from a regression, where the paper fits a surface to the density of all pairs; pairs without a peak within 70 ms are dropped.

outcomes.statement: During MS cooling the theta time lags between place cell pairs increased compared with before and after cooling (P = 8e-5 and P = 0.00032), and did not differ between before and after (P = 0.79).
outcomes.source: Results, MS temperature effects on theta time/phase compression of place cells sequences, paragraph 3; Figure 5H
outcomes.quote: During MS cooling, the time lags increased significantly ... whereas they were not different from each other during precooling and post-cooling sessions (P = 0.79)
outcomes.notes: Under reading (a), cooling against pre over 3136 pairs (30.5 against 28.5 ms, P = 1.14e-06) and against post (P = 1.3e-10); pre and post do not differ (P = 0.0967). Reading (b) agrees (P = 0.023, 0.016 and 0.81), and so does the half-period window (P = 3.8e-22 and 2.0e-29).
deviations: The legend's n = 10 sessions cannot give P = 8e-5 with a signed-rank test over sessions, so the test over pairs was taken as the main reading.

outcomes.statement: Theta phase lags between place cell pairs were not affected by MS cooling (P > 0.24 between all conditions).
outcomes.source: Results, MS temperature effects on theta time/phase compression of place cells sequences, paragraph 3; Figure 5I
outcomes.quote: In contrast, phase lags between spikes of place cell pairs were not affected by MS cooling (Fig. 5i; P > 0.24 between all conditions).
outcomes.notes: Phase lags are slightly larger during cooling than before (1.367 against 1.304 rad, mean difference 0.051 rad, P = 0.0015) and after (P = 0.0043); pre and post do not differ (P = 0.51). Per session medians, cooling against pre P = 0.062. The +-pi window spans about 1.15 periods of the phase correlogram (1.74 pi). With the lag picked within +-pi/2 (a variant), 43.3% of pre pairs get another lag or none, and cooling is still above pre (mean difference 0.025 rad, P = 0.0196) but not above post (P = 0.162); pre and post do not differ (P = 0.178). Part of the increase may come from how the lag is picked.

outcomes.statement: The fraction of place cells active in a theta cycle was not significantly affected by MS cooling (P = 0.2).
outcomes.source: Results, MS temperature effects on theta time/phase compression of place cells sequences, paragraph 4; Figure 5J
outcomes.quote: we found that the fraction of place cells active in a given theta cycle was not significantly affected by MS cooling (Fig. 5j; P = 0.2).
outcomes.notes: The fraction active is higher during cooling (0.2405 against 0.226, rank-sum P = 1.5e-22 over 9037 and 10152 cycles). Per session the cooling mean is lower than pre in 5 of 9 sessions (P = 0.734); cooling against post gives P = 0.074 and pre against post P = 0.004. Session means range from 0.159 to 0.315 and sessions contribute different numbers of cycles in each state, so the pooled test reflects the make-up of the pool as much as an effect. Cycles are longer during cooling (131.1 ms against 117.8 and 117.2 ms).
deviations: The paper does not name its test; the default rank-sum test over cycles was fixed before the analysis.

outcomes.statement: The number of spikes emitted by all neurons per theta cycle was preserved during MS cooling (P > 0.058 between all conditions).
outcomes.source: Results, MS temperature effects on theta time/phase compression of place cells sequences, paragraph 4; Figure 5K
outcomes.quote: The number of spikes emitted by all neurons per theta cycle was also preserved after MS cooling (Fig. 5k)
outcomes.notes: Pre and cooling do not differ (45.68 and 44.98 spikes, P = 0.0758), but post (51.68) differs from both (P below 1e-50). Per session, cooling differs from neither pre (P = 0.57) nor post (P = 0.129), and post differs from pre (P = 0.02). Session means range from 17.66 to 91.37 spikes, so the pooled tests depend on how many cycles each session contributes.
deviations: Spikes of all good and good2 units; the paper's 'all neurons' may include other units.

outcomes.statement: Hippocampal temperature fell by less than 1.5 C at the time of the largest MS temperature decrease, and later than the MS cooling.
outcomes.source: Results, MS cooling decreases hippocampal theta frequency and power, paragraph 3 (Supplementary Figure 1H to 1K)
outcomes.quote: we measured temperature simultaneously in the MS and hippocampus, and found < 1.5° C decrease in the hippocampus at the time of the largest MS temperature decrease ... the mild temperature decrease in the hippocampus was considerably delayed
outcomes.notes: The control experiment that measured temperature in the MS and both hippocampi is not in the dandiset, whose files hold only the MS temperature of the 50 behavioural sessions. The data check lists every series in all 100 files, and the only temperature series is processing/behavior/Temperature. The paper's data statement points to the lab website and CRCNS; no other DANDI deposit of these recordings was found.

findings.statement: The temperature series of the nine MS10 sessions and of the two control sessions of 2018-07-19 (MS21 and MS22) is not a recording. The paper's code lists no temperature channel for these sessions. In the files ten of them run from 17.0 to 37.0 C (exactly in nine; MS10-170313 reaches 16.98 C) and sit at exactly 37.0 C for 16% to 35% of samples, and MS10-170307 is a constant 37.0 C, while no recorded trace repeats its maximum. Nothing in the files says the series is modelled.

The two sessions of 2018-07-19, which the paper's code lists as controls without cooling (cooling_session 0, no onsets), have trials labelled Pre-Cooling, Cooling on, Cooling off and Post-Cooling and a temperature dip; their theta frequency during 'Cooling on' differs from pre by -0.20 and +0.44 Hz, against a median of -0.82 Hz in the cooled sessions.

Six of the paper's 53 behavioural sessions are not in the dandiset (MS12-170712, MS12-170715, MS13-171204, MS13-171205, MS13-171206, MS21-180806); four of them were in version 0.210812.1514 as files without behaviour.
MS21-180627 has trials without the cooling state and MS21-180712 has no trials, so two more of the paper's sessions cannot be used for the cooling comparisons.

The files hold no cell types, no place field definitions and no electrode locations (every location is 'unknown'), so the putative pyramidal cells and interneurons and the place fields of the paper have to be made again.
The trial state 'Cooling off' (a median 14 trials per session between cooling and recovery) is not described in the files or the paper.
In seven sessions (the six MS10 sessions with units and MS12-170723) every unit has quality 'unsorted', so no curated unit can be selected; MS10 has no usable units.

In MS21-180621 and MS22-180621 the units carry no spatial information (0.23 and 0.12 bits/spike, the same as with spikes shifted by 60 s), although they are locked to theta, so the clock of spikes and position could not be established there.

The dandiset holds three sessions that are not in the paper's behavioural analysis (the two 2018-07-19 controls and MS10-170307, whose temperature is constant) without saying so; they carry the same cooling labels as the analysed sessions.
The first published version (0.210812.1514) has no trials table in its files, so the cooling states and choice errors are only in the later versions.
The Methods give position tracking at 120 Hz; the MS10 sessions are sampled at 40 Hz (six), 30 Hz (one) and 120 Hz (two).

The legend of Figure 5H gives P = 8.0e-5 by a sign rank test with N = 10 sessions; an exact signed-rank test over 10 sessions cannot give a P below 0.002, so the test must be over pairs or the N refers to something else.

The Discussion gives a 12% decrease of LFP theta frequency during cooling, while the Results give within-field LFP theta of 8.4 Hz before and 7.7 Hz during cooling, a decrease of about 8%, which this attempt reproduces (9% over trials).

entries.name: 000059-petersen-2020
entries.title: Cooling of the medial septum, hippocampal theta and place cell timing (Petersen & Buzsaki 2020)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Petersen and Buzsaki (2020) on dandiset 000059, which holds 50 sessions of five rats running a spatial alternation task on a figure-8 maze while the medial septum was cooled, with MS temperature, trials, position, LFP, wide-band data and sorted units. It tests the slowing of theta with temperature, the increase of choice errors, the oscillation frequency of place cells against LFP theta, place field features, and the time and phase lags of place cell pairs. The hippocampal temperature recordings of the control experiment are not in the dandiset.
